q: Are electric vehicle deliveries zero emission in my Scope 3?
title: Are EV deliveries zero in Scope 3?
short: No. An electric delivery has no tailpipe emissions, but the electricity that charged the vehicle was generated somewhere, and in India most of it from coal. Your Scope 3 transport figure is the carrier's kWh times the grid factor, which is lower than diesel but not zero.
audience: Brands and D2C exporters using EV last-mile partners

sections.h: Where EV deliveries sit in your inventory
p: Deliveries you pay a carrier for, inbound or out to customers, are Scope 3 Category 4, upstream transportation. Deliveries you do not pay for, such as a marketplace's own logistics, are Category 9. The vehicle's charging electricity is in the carrier's Scope 2; in yours it shows up as transport emissions.

ol: Get the energy used: kWh per km for the vehicle type from the carrier or the manufacturer, and the km driven for your shipments.
Multiply km x kWh per km to get kWh.
Multiply by the grid factor for where the vehicle was charged, 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25 for India from the CEA CO2 Baseline Database, version 21.0.
If the carrier shares only total kWh for a shared fleet, ask how it allocates to your parcels, by weight, parcel count or distance.

p: ISO 14083:2023 and the GLEC Framework count the energy supply of a transport chain, so electricity generation is part of an EV's transport emissions, the same way diesel production is part of a diesel van's on a well-to-wheel basis. They also count hub and warehouse energy between legs. A carrier quoting zero is reporting tailpipe only.

sections.h: Claims to check before you repeat them
ul: Carbon-neutral delivery usually means the carrier bought offsets. Offsets are reported separately and do not reduce your Scope 3 figure.
Solar-charged fleets: ask for evidence, such as on-site generation records or certificates covering the kWh. If the carrier cannot show it, use the grid factor.
Do not write zero-emission delivery on your packaging or website on the basis of EVs alone.

example.title: Illustrative: one month with a shared EV fleet
lines: Carrier's fleet charging for the month: 24,000 kWh across 60,000 parcels (assumed figures)
Your parcels: 9,000, so your share is 24,000 x 9,000 / 60,000 = 3,600 kWh
3,600 x 0.710 = 2,556 kg CO2 for the month
Per parcel: 2,556 / 9,000 = 0.284 kg CO2, where the carrier's report said zero
example.note: This allocates by parcel count. If your parcels are heavier or travel further than the fleet average, ask the carrier to allocate by weight or distance instead.

senseible: Senseible applies the CEA grid factor of 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25 to electricity and reads freight invoices into a separate supplier evidence trail. It does not get kWh from a carrier's fleet; that has to come from the carrier, and the same factor then applies.
